rule: Base capsules may show only game artwork, the game name and an official subtitle: no review scores of any kind, no award names, symbols or logos, no discount copy and no other text.
check: manual (image content; corpus only has image URLs)

rule: Temporary text such as a sale or update banner belongs only in a Capsule Artwork Override with an expiry date, not in the base capsule.
check: manual
note: Max override length: the rules page snippet said 14 days, older copies and third-party guides say one month / 30 days. Verify on the live page.

rule: Use the current capsule sizes (header 920x430, small 462x174, main 1232x706); Valve raised the sizes in August 2024 and no longer accepts the old dimensions.
check: headerImage present; capsuleImage present (null means missing). Pixel size is manual unless the image is fetched.
note: 920x430 and 462x174 seen in the Steamworks assets overview; 1232x706 seen only in third-party guides that say they checked the live docs.

rule: The logo must stay legible on the small capsule, whose 120x45 and 184x69 variants Steam generates automatically from the 462x174 image, so design (recrop) the small capsule rather than shrinking the header.
check: manual (view the 462x174 capsule at 120 and 184 px wide)

rule: Capsule art should make the genre recognisable instantly; a capsule whose genre isn't clear at small size is a common failure.
check: manual

rule: Provide library assets: a 600x900 library capsule with logo and artwork, a 3840x1240 library hero with artwork only (no text), and a PNG library logo 1280 px wide and/or 720 px tall.
check: manual (library assets aren't in store appdetails data)

rule: The short description is plain text limited to a few hundred characters (the editor counter is about 300); use the space, and leave room for translations, which are truncated if they run over.
check: shortDescription.length: warn if < ~150 or empty; compare to comps' median length
note: Valve's docs say 'a few hundred characters'; the ~300 figure is from third-party guides citing the editor's counter.

rule: The short description should state the genre and the player's primary action, then the hook, without going deep into story or setting.
check: auto heuristic: first sentence of shortDescription contains a top-3 tag or genre word; low ratio of lore words

rule: Avoid over-generalised verbs such as 'battle evil' or 'save the world'; if swapping in the genre's biggest game name still makes the description true, it isn't distinctive.
check: auto heuristic: flag stock phrases in shortDescription

rule: Break the About section into subheads, one per primary beat of the game's loop, because shoppers skim and mostly skip the long description.
check: manual (corpus aboutText is plain text; headers are lost) or count paragraph breaks in aboutText

rule: Use short animated GIFs (or WEBP/MP4/WEBM) in the About section to show key action; animations only play in the About and Special Announcement sections, and alt text is supported and localisable.
check: manual (aboutText is plain text)

rule: Include a features list near the bottom of the About section.
check: auto heuristic: aboutText contains a 'features' heading or list-like lines
note: Zukowski's checklist says Valve usually rejects store pages without one; not confirmed in Valve's own text.

rule: Upload at least five screenshots, widescreen 16:9, at least 1920x1080.
check: screenshots.length >= 5 (compare to comps' median); resolution manual unless the URL or image is inspected

rule: Screenshots should show only gameplay: no concept art, pre-rendered stills, awards or marketing text, which belong in the store page's own spaces.
check: manual

rule: Order screenshots so the first four sell the game: the hover tooltip in search and lists rotates through the first four screenshots, not the trailer.
check: manual (order); auto: at least 4 screenshots exist
note: One guide says the first two; the Game Developer user study says four.

rule: At least one early screenshot should show UI that makes the genre obvious.
check: manual

rule: Make the first trailer mostly gameplay from the player's perspective; Steam builds the micro trailer from six 1-second clips of the first video, so logos and cutaways there leak into it.
check: movies >= 1 (auto); content manual

rule: Only two trailers can appear before the screenshots, so pick the two strongest and put the rest after.
check: movies count (auto, info only); order manual

rule: Show gameplay within the first few seconds of the trailer and make the opening work without sound.
check: manual
note: Exact seconds (3, 5 or 10) and the 60-90 s length are industry conventions, not Valve rules.

rule: Fill the tag list: only the top 20 tags are shown and used by Steam for visibility.
check: tags.length >= 20 (auto)

rule: The top five tags should give a clear picture of the game, and the first 15 should be sorted by relevance because some store filters only look at them.
check: auto: top-5 tags include the main genre tags shared with comps; specific genre tags rank above generic ones (Indie, Singleplayer, 2D)

rule: Remove tags that don't accurately reflect the game's content, theme or nature; similar-game recommendations depend on overlap between tags more than their order.
check: auto heuristic: tags rare among comps and absent from the description; manual confirm

rule: Re-check tags after launch, because players also apply tags and the weights shift over time.
check: manual (reminder; compare votes over time if history is kept)

rule: Study the leading game in your genre (its tags, UI conventions and gameplay verbs) and mirror the relevant ones on your page.
check: auto: overlap of target tags with the top comps' tags

rule: Localise both the store page and the game where possible; Steam treats store-page and in-game localization separately and recommends both.
check: languages.length vs comps' median (auto); store-page translation manual

rule: Only fully supported Steam languages are translated across the Steam client, store and community; 'game support only' languages aren't supported in Steamworks APIs.
check: auto: languages are valid Steam language names

rule: Text on images must be localised into the languages the game supports, so keep text off images or upload localised versions.
check: manual

rule: Set prices in all of Steam's currencies (37) using the pricing tool's recommended regional prices as the starting point, rather than one USD price converted at market rates.
check: manual (corpus has USD only); auto: priceUSD vs comps' median

rule: A launch discount must be set up before release, runs 7 to 14 days, and Valve generally suggests 10% to 15%.
check: manual (prelaunch reminder)

rule: No discount is allowed for 30 days after a base-price increase in any currency, so finalise prices before launch and sales.
check: manual

rule: Discounts must be at least 10% (and at most 90%), and there's a cooldown between discounts that doesn't apply to the four major seasonal sales.
check: manual
note: 2022 coverage gives a 28-day cooldown; current docs mention 30-day rules elsewhere. Verify the live number.

rule: Below 10 user reviews Steam shows no review score ('Need more user reviews to generate a score'), so plan to reach 10 reviews quickly after launch.
check: reviews.total < 10 (auto)

rule: Review labels need volume as well as ratio: 'Very Positive' needs 80%+ with 50+ reviews, and 'Overwhelmingly Positive' needs 95%+ with 500+.
check: reviews.total and reviews.positivePct (auto, info)
note: Third-party table. Claims that 10/50/500 reviews unlock algorithmic visibility are disputed (firstlook.gg calls it a myth).

rule: As a benchmark, Zukowski says a game that doesn't reach about 250 reviews in its first month rarely breaks out later.
check: reviews.total vs days since releaseDate (auto, info only)

rule: Put the Steam page up as soon as you start showing the game publicly, so that every bit of attention can become a wishlist.
check: comingSoon true and page exists (auto); timing manual

rule: A Coming Soon page must be live at least two weeks before release, and should be submitted for review at least 7 business days before you want it public.
check: comingSoon + releaseDate (auto: warn if release within 14 days and page just went live)

rule: Once the page is live and the release date is within 14 days, the date can't be changed without contacting Valve.
check: releaseDate within 14 days of today (auto, info)

rule: The release date can be shown as an exact date, a month, a quarter, a year, or 'Coming Soon'; show the most precise window you can commit to.
check: releaseDate string: exact / month / quarter / year / 'Coming soon' (auto, info)

rule: Reaching Steam's Popular Upcoming list is estimated to take roughly 7,000 wishlists, with velocity and closeness to the release date also counting.
check: manual (wishlists are private); followers can be a rough proxy
note: An estimate from third-party guides attributing it to Zukowski, not a Valve figure.

rule: A demo is a separate App ID shown as a button on the main page; when it first becomes playable you can notify everyone who wishlisted the game (one notification, with a two-week cooldown per App ID), so launch the demo deliberately.
check: hasDemo (auto)

rule: Disable achievements in the demo and grant them in the full game after purchase.
check: manual

rule: A game can appear in only one Steam Next Fest, needs a published public store page and a publicly playable demo by the start, and the demo should go to build review at least 3 weeks ahead; pick the edition closest before launch.
check: comingSoon && hasDemo (auto: eligible); edition choice manual

rule: Next Fest wishlists pay off: per Valve data reported by GameDiscoverCo, the median released game saw a 292% increase in converting wishlists made during Next Fest versus the two weeks before.
check: manual (info)

rule: Tick every supported OS on the Basic Info tab and fill in its system requirements before publishing.
check: manual (not in the corpus; could add pc_requirements from appdetails)

rule: Request a Steam Deck compatibility review from the app's Technical Tools; the Verified, Playable or Unsupported result is shown on the store page.
check: manual

rule: Complete all three content survey sections (general, mature content, generative AI) honestly before review; the answers decide how the game appears against each customer's content preferences, and some can't be edited later without Steam Support.
check: manual (content_descriptors exist in appdetails if fetched)

rule: Keep one, at most two, events visible on the store page at a time, archive old ones, and use the patch-notes type for small updates so major updates stand out.
check: manual

rule: Reserve event featuring in the Library for major events, with adequate time between them.
check: manual
note: No source gave a specific update cadence; Steamworks has an 'Update Visibility Rounds' page that wasn't readable from here.
